summary:
This blog serves as both a philosophical manifesto and a technical resource for the transition from traditional software architecture to AI-native applications. It explores the concept of the "post-app" era, arguing that software containers are a historical glitch and advocating for intent-based, context-aware computing. The content ranges from high-level essays defining "AI-native" versus "AI-forced" design to in-depth discussions on open-source infrastructure that unifies fragmented data silos into intelligent endpoints.

Beyond theory, the blog provides practical guides for developers and business leaders navigating the complexities of AI adoption. It covers technical tutorials on building Agentic RAG systems, managing UI states for generative flows, and utilizing low-code tools like Appsmith. Through case studies and explainer posts, it demonstrates how Unbody's platform allows users to bypass the overhead of building custom AI engines, enabling the rapid deployment of autonomous agents and knowledge bases.
suggestiveQuestions: What is the difference between an AI-native application and an AI-forced one?
Why is the era of standalone software containers and apps coming to an end?
How can I build an Agentic RAG system that understands nuanced user queries?
What are the risks and costs associated with building in-house AI infrastructure?
How should UI state management change to accommodate generative data flows?
How can businesses unify scattered data from platforms like Google Drive into a single AI endpoint?
What are the benefits of using an open-source, modular backend for AI development?
